Don't worry about it. The point of a liberal arts degree usually isn't to find work in that specific field so much as it is to enhance you as an individual. English is a tremendously flexible degree that is valuable to most any enterprise when applied correctly; moreover, like other liberal arts degrees it equips you with skills in research, analysis and communication, as well as enriching your understanding of the world around you.

Besides, too much emphasis has been put on using one's education to get a job. Yes, it's important to be secure, pay the bills and have money to live comfortably, but by the same token, we should work to live, not the other way around. I think as a society we ought to place more value on education for its own sake, and not simply treat it as a means to an end.
